{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (we represent Corio, the Customer/licensee)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.5 — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings. The commercial shape is favourable to us in several important respects: the Section 8 infringement indemnity is one‑way in our favour and, because Section 9 excepts liability under Section 8 from both the cap and the consequential‑damages waiver, it is uncapped. There is no exclusivity, non‑compete, MFN, minimum‑commitment or liquidated‑damages obligation on us; the audit right in Section 4.4 already matches our preferred position; renewals are one‑year with a 30‑day opt‑out; and Section 14.1 lets us assign to a successor on M&A without consent.

Five issues need to be negotiated. Three are critical or structural: (i) the Section 9 cap is measured only by amounts we actually paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to," which slices the cap down to a single transaction and can fall well below six months' fees, with confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct all inside the cap; (ii) Section 13.5 transfers ownership of Corio‑created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back; and (iii) Section 11.3 permits outright destruction of our data at Commerce One's election, with no return obligation, format, deadline or certification. In addition, the licence grant does not reach our affiliates or contractors and has no mechanism to add them; there is no customer termination‑for‑convenience right in a five‑year term; the Product Warranty Period runs only 60 days from the Effective Date and is hard‑capped at 31 December 1999, so it can expire on or before acceptance; and there is no vendor insurance clause at all.

One finding (non‑solicitation) failed verification and is carried as **needs review** rather than as a conclusion.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (exceeds fallback) | § 8 Indemnification |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13.5 Shared Resources |
| 3 | Critical | LOL‑CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve‑outs | **Deviation** | § 9 Limitation of Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant (at fallback) | § 14.1 Miscellaneous |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 2 Grant of Rights |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 11 Term and Termination |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of Rights |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non‑compete on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 13 Shared Resources |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 Term and Termination |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 4.4 Fees |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (at fallback) | § 14.3 Miscellaneous |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most‑favoured‑nation burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | Exhibit B Pricing |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Compliant (preferred) | § 4 Fees |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non‑solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review** (verification failed) | Exhibit D Sales and Marketing Cooperation |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto‑renewal and notice window | Compliant (preferred) | § 11.1 Term and Termination |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11 Term and Termination |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 Miscellaneous |

### Deviations and missing terms — what we propose

- **§ 9 Limitation of liability (critical).** The cap is limited to amounts actually paid by Corio in the prior twelve months "for the transaction which the liability relates to," and the only carve‑out is Section 8. We propose a mutual cap of the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, measured from the event giving rise to liability, and an "Excluded Claims" definition covering Section 8 indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud. The mutual consequential‑damages exclusion stays as drafted. Note p0092 appears to be an OCR duplicate of the same sentences across a page break; the conformed text should be reconciled to the edited p0090.
- **§ 13.5 Ownership (critical).** Delete only the "unless supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" carve‑out so that Corio owns Developments it creates solely. Commerce One's pre‑existing materials and its Software ownership under Section 2.8 are untouched. If ongoing support is the real concern, a support licence to Commerce One is our sensible fallback.
- **§ 2 Licence scope (high).** Insert a new Section 2.11 extending the Section 2 licences to Corio's affiliates and to contractors acting on Corio's behalf, with Corio responsible for their compliance. "Affiliate" appears nowhere in the Agreement and there is no mechanism to add one.
- **§ 11 Termination for convenience (high).** Add a Corio right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro‑rata refund of prepaid recurring fees and no early‑termination penalty, inserted after 11.2 (existing 11.3 renumbers). We are content that Commerce One has no mid‑term convenience right and would confirm that in the same insert.
- **§ 11 Transition and data return (medium).** Insert a new Section 11.4 requiring return of Corio, Customer and Software User data within 30 days in a machine‑readable format, then deletion with written certification, plus six months' transition assistance at then‑current rates (90 days acceptable as a fallback). The surviving licence and support provisions in 11.3 and 5.3, and the Section 12 escrow, are left in place — they already exceed our preferred position.
- **§ 7 Warranty duration (medium).** Extend the Product Warranty Period to twelve months from acceptance (fallback: 90 days from acceptance). Remedies and exclusions are left untouched; the issue is solely that the current 60‑day/31‑December‑1999 period can expire on or before acceptance testing completes under Section 3.1.
- **§ 14 Insurance (missing, low).** Insert the preferred vendor coverage package as a new Section 14.10, renumbering Complete Understanding to 14.11.

---

## 3. Walk‑away items

These are the points our findings place in, or adjacent to, walk‑away territory. We should not sign without movement on them:

1. **Per‑transaction liability cap (§ 9).** A cap measured by the fees for the single transaction to which the liability relates can fall well below six months' fees — walk‑away territory for a vendor cap. Compounding this, confidentiality (§ 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap.
2. **Destruction of our data on exit (§ 11.3).** The exit wording permits outright destruction of our data at Commerce One's election, with no return obligation. Our findings treat that as walk‑away territory and it fails the fallback (export within 30 days).
3. **Assignment of our work product to the Vendor (§ 13.5).** The support carve‑out assigns Corio‑created Developments to Commerce One with no licence back, failing both the preferred and fallback positions on a material term.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the five deviations and the missing insurance clause: § 9 cap and Excluded Claims; § 13.5 carve‑out deletion; new § 2.11 affiliates/contractors; § 11 Corio convenience right; new § 11.4 data return, deletion certification and transition assistance; § 7 warranty period; new § 14.10 insurance with renumbering of Complete Understanding.
2. **Resolve the non‑solicitation finding (verification failed).** Re‑run the check before we rely on the conclusion that no personnel covenant binds us. Separately, the NDA executed concurrently and integrated by § 14.10 was not available for review and should be obtained and checked for a buried non‑solicit. If Commerce One later proposes a personnel covenant, our position is the fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of involvement, services personnel only, general‑advertising and unsolicited‑approach carve‑outs, no no‑hire.
3. Reconcile the p0092 / p0090 OCR duplication in Section 9 so the conformed text reflects the edited page only.
4. Confirm internally the negotiating priority: items 1–3 in the walk‑away list first; the licence‑scope, convenience‑right, warranty‑duration and insurance items are worth pressing but are tradeable.
5. No action on the compliant findings. We note for the record, without redlining, that the assignment clause (§ 14.1) and governing law (§ 14.3, California law with AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco) sit at the fallback rather than the preferred position, and that the audit clause lacks a fixed notice period; we would not spend capital on any of these."}
